sections.html: Needlefishes (Belonidae) are a relatively small family of about 35 species, found in marine and freshwater habitats of temperate and tropical regions worldwide. The genus Xenentodon is restricted to tropical Asia and is found exclusively in freshwater. Currently only two species are accepted: Xenentodon cancila and X. canciloides. The fish imported from Thailand are closer to X. canciloides than to X. cancila, but may represent a still undescribed species.
The genus Xenentodon is restricted to tropical Asia. The imported fish originate from Thailand.
These are very elegant predators that live near the water surface. In their natural habitat they are always found in schools.
Xenentodon can reach a total length of up to 30 cm and thus should not be kept in too small tanks.
Aquarists must guarantee a supply of small live food fish. If this is ensured, keeping needlefish is unproblematic.
Males can be recognized when they reach sexual maturity (at a length of 15-20 cm): from that size on they have a red hump directly behind the head.
They breed readily in captivity. The eggs have entangling tendrils and are placed in fine water plants and similar. The fish do not care for their brood in any way.

Xenentodon: ancient Greek, meaning "with disconcerting teeth"; this applies to the lower pharyngeal plate. cancila: after an indigenous name for the fish in Bengal. canciloides: means "similar to cancila". Suggested common name: Inkstripe Needlefish.
